requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged across execution and restart. The restoration used the platform's existing tar and standard shell utilities; the command record shows no software installation or platform replacement.

overall_summary: All task outcomes are satisfied with direct byte, mode, selectivity, preservation, and platform checks. The mandatory restart protocol is also complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered system and data state. Hygiene is strong aside from one leftover reboot log in /tmp.
limitations: Native package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently observed.
Lifecycle snapshots did not inventory the task's live file tree; final file-state conclusions rely on direct executor commands, including comprehensive post-restart validation.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required extraction and provider-wide restart were bounded and directly supported restoration and recovery evidence. The initial unprivileged extraction failed without changing the live tree, so it is not penalized. One unnecessary mutation remained: cmd-8f49bc5a1374486a redirected reboot output to /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, and the lifecycle snapshot confirms that temporary file was not removed. No failed services, new listeners, package operations, or other unrelated mutations were observed.
